title: SDK exception patterns, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
We need a consistent, cross-language pattern for how Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) surface runtime errors, classify retryability, and present ergonomic streaming APIs. Current SDKs differ in exception types, error codes, and guidance on client retry/backoff. This causes developer confusion and hidden failure modes in production (e.g. retries that should not occur, or unrecoverable streaming termination being retried).

Goals:
- Define a small, language-idiomatic exception/error type hierarchy that captures: transient/retryable, permanent/fatal, user-code/input, authentication/authorization, rate-limited, quota-exceeded, model-internal/quality-regressions, streaming-terminal vs streaming-recoverable events.
- Standardize a machine-readable error code space (string codes) and map to HTTP/gRPC/transport semantics.
- Provide clear retry guidance in SDKs and surface retryable hint metadata to callers (e.g., should_retry: boolean, retry_after seconds, backoff_hint).
- Improve streaming ergonomics: differentiate between recoverable partial-stream failures, terminal stream errors, and graceful end-of-stream. Offer helper abstractions to resume or fail-fast where possible.
- Include examples and migration notes for existing users.

Non-goals:
- Change server-side HTTP status semantics beyond well-defined mappings. We will map existing server statuses to our codes, not alter server behavior.

Proposed design (high-level):
1) Error code space (string codes):
   - RW_AUTH_ERROR (auth/credentials invalid)
   - RW_PERMISSIONS_ERROR (SAML/SSO/ACL)
   - RW_RATE_LIMITED (global rate limit triggered)
   - RW_QUOTA_EXCEEDED (customer quota)
   - RW_TRANSIENT (network/infra blip, safe-to-retry)
   - RW_BACKEND_OVERLOADED (capacity / 429 at routing layer, retryable with backoff)
   - RW_INVALID_REQUEST (client proto/payload validation)
   - RW_MODEL_DEGRADATION (model produced corrupted or missing output; not retryable by default)
   - RW_STREAM_ABORTED (server terminated stream unexpectedly; retry may be allowed for idempotent requests)
   - RW_STREAM_PARTIAL_ERROR (non-terminal; server emits an error event but stream may continue)

2) Standard SDK error fields (present on error objects across languages):
   - code: string (one of above)
   - message: human-friendly message
   - http_status: integer (when applicable)
   - should_retry: boolean (recommended by server/runtime)
   - retry_after: seconds as float (optional)
   - request_id: string (trace id)
   - details: string|map (free text or opaque metadata) -- SDK will keep as string in top-level JSON fields; language bindings may expose richer typed details where idiomatic

3) Language-specific shapes (examples):
   Python:
     - Base class: RedwoodError(Exception)
     - Subclasses: AuthError(RedwoodError), RateLimitError(RedwoodError), TransientError(RedwoodError), PermanentError(RedwoodError), StreamingError(RedwoodError)
     - Instances carry attrs: code, http_status, should_retry, retry_after, request_id, details

   TypeScript:
     - Interface RedwoodError { name: string; code: string; message: string; httpStatus?: number; shouldRetry?: boolean; retryAfter?: number; requestId?: string; details?: string }
     - Error constructors: new RedwoodErrorImpl(props) extends Error

   Go:
     - Type RedwoodError struct { Code string; Message string; HTTPStatus int; ShouldRetry bool; RetryAfter float64; RequestID string; Details string }
     - helper funcs: IsRetryable(err) bool, AsRedwoodError(err) *RedwoodError

4) Retry semantics: mapping and recommended client behavior
   - RW_TRANSIENT, RW_BACKEND_OVERLOADED: should_retry=true. Use exponential backoff + jitter. Default max attempts: 4. Respect server-provided retry_after if present.
   - RW_RATE_LIMITED: should_retry=true but honor Retry-After / retry_after header. Consider client throttling.
   - RW_AUTH_ERROR, RW_PERMISSIONS_ERROR, RW_INVALID_REQUEST, RW_MODEL_DEGRADATION: should_retry=false. Surface actionable message.

5) Streaming ergonomics:
   - Server will emit terminal error event with code RW_STREAM_ABORTED when it cannot continue. SDK streaming consumers must receive a typed exception (StreamingError) with code and request_id.
   - For non-terminal issues, server can emit RW_STREAM_PARTIAL_ERROR; SDK should expose event callbacks for partial errors (on_partial_error) while keeping stream open.
   - Provide a high-level retry helper for streaming that will attempt resumable calls for idempotent streaming workloads (examples below).

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec document reviewed by SDK leads (Python, TS, Go) and infra/runtime.
- SDK prototypes implemented in feature branches with consistent error object shape.
- Backward-compatibility tests: existing simple error handling code should continue to function; new fields optional.
- Integration tests cover mapping between server HTTP statuses and SDK codes, and streaming partial/terminal flows.
- Docs and migration guide published on Docs + CHANGELOG entries.

Migration notes for existing users:
- Existing SDK errors may be a superset; new RedwoodError types are additive. Consumers who use string matching on error messages must be migrated to use error.code or helper matchers (IsRetryable, IsAuthError).
- For streaming, users who previously treated any stream close as an Exception should opt into on_partial_error to handle non-terminal events.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Finalize spec (this ticket).
- Week 2-3: Implement Python and TS prototypes; add test harness mapping server errors to SDK codes.
- Week 4: Implement Go support and publish beta SDKs with opt-in flag (e.g., RedwoodConfig.enable_new_error_model=true).
- Week 5: Collect usage/telemetry, address issues, flip default in SDKs in next minor release.

Telemetry/metrics to collect post-rollout:
- Percentage of errors carrying code field.
- Distribution of codes observed in production.
- Number of client retries triggered by should_retry=true.
- Streaming partial vs terminal error rates.

Links and artifacts:
- Design notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/Unified+Error+Design
- Proto mappings draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2841 (draft PR)
- Example SDK prototypes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-prototypes/tree/err-model-34122

Implementation risks and trade-offs:
- Adding fields increases SDK surface; we keep fields optional to preserve compatibility.
- Relying on server to set should_retry may be imperfect; SDKs will also implement local heuristics for network-level failures.
- Streaming resume semantics are only possible for idempotent or resumable request types; we will not attempt to resume non-idempotent generation by default.

Notes for reviewers:
- Please validate proposed codes: are there gaps for enterprise errors (e.g., tenant-level policy denies)?
- Language leads: confirm class/interface names and whether helper matchers (IsRetryable) fit idiomatic patterns.
